observations.summary: The reliability of the reported Cash in Bank - Local Currency, Current Account (CIB - LCCA) account amounting to P8.072 billion is unreliable due to the following: a. Existence of outstanding reconciling items in the Bank Reconciliation Statement (BRS) totaling P155.799 million and P142.181 million for additions and deductions, respectively, which remain unadjusted in the books; b. Existence of variance totaling P96.510 million between the Subsidiary Ledgers (SL) balance of the OCAT and cashbook balance of the City Treasurer's Office (CTO); and P160.925 million between the SL and the confirmed balances from Authorized Government Depository Banks (AGDBs); and c. Existence of bank accounts for expropriated properties that were opened and confirmed by the bank as savings accounts and were recorded as CIB - LCCA under the General Fund (GF) books totaling P145.025 million. The above conditions resulted in the misstatement of affected accounts contrary to Paragraph 27 of International Public Sector Accounting Standard (IPSAS) 1, Item 3.0 of COA Circular No. 96-011 and Section 20 of COA Circular No. 92-382 dated July 3, 1992.

rows.recommendation: 1.17. We recommended that Management require: a. The CTO to: •Immediately forward to the OCAT the supporting documents for the recording of necessary adjusting entries; •Regularly coordinate with the OCAT to facilitate reconciliation of cashbook balances with the OCAT SLs for CIB accounts; and •Promptly communicate noted discrepancies with the OCAT so adjustments, if any, can be recorded in a timely manner both in the books and BRS. b. The OCAT to: •Ensure that BRS are prepared for all active bank accounts and reconciling items identified in the reports are promptly recorded in the books; and •Ensure that identified reconciling items in the BRS are immediately adjusted in the books to prevent accumulation of unadjusted variances between records of the OCAT, CTO and AGDB balances.
rows.action_plan: The CTO committed to furnish the OCAT with the reconciling items reflected in their cash books for reconciliation of CAD records.
rows.person_responsible: Office of the City Accountant (OCAT) & City Treasurer's Office (CTO)
rows.status_text: Not Implemented Not Implemented Not Implemented Not Implemented Not Implemented
rows.remarks: Reconciliation is still ongoing. No adjusting entry has been made yet by OCAT as of June 30, 2025 (latest FS submitted), while coordination between OCAT and CTO is likewise still in progress..
rows.citation: CY 2024 APMT, CY 2024 Observation No. 1, p. 2

observations.summary: There were deficiencies in the grant and liquidation of cash advances, contrary to COA regulations to wit: a. Cash advances amounting to P355.158 million remained unliquidated as of December 31, 2024, due to the non-submission of liquidation reports by Accountable Officers (AOs), contrary to Section 89 of PD No. 1445 and Sections 5.1.1, 5.1.3, 5.7 and 5.8 of COA Circular No. 97-002; b. Cash Advances required for immediate liquidation and settlement totaling P106.136 million pertained to accounts of AOs who are already deceased, resigned, retired or separated from the City that have been aged two months to 19 years, contrary to Section 4.1.3 of COA Circular No. 97-002 dated February 10, 1997; and

rows.recommendation: We recommended that Management: a. Direct all concerned AOs to submit the liquidation reports with supporting documents (SDs) for all outstanding CAs by issuing demand letters particularly for due and demandable advances as of December 31, 2024; b. Ensure that O&E who will retire, resign or transfer to other agencies settle their accountabilities before issuing them clearance certificates. Ascertain the actual employment status of those with no information as to whether they are still active or already separated from the service; and
rows.action_plan: The OCAT justified that they have made efforts to reach out to those who have already resigned and separated from service but unfortunately, they have not received responses. For the cash advances related to the deceased employees, the OCAT have already submitted a formal request for write-off. Further, they committed that they are working with the liquidation of the active Accountable Officers and will enhance their monitoring system to enforce stricter compliance with regulations. The OCAT averred that they are reviewing and strengthening the internal policies on cash advances to ensure that no new cash advances will be granted without liquidating the previous issued. In summary, the OCAT committed to
rows.remarks: Pending appropriate action from Management. Pending appropriate action from Management.

observations.summary: The accuracy, existence and completeness of various receivables accounts as of December 31, 2024, cannot be ascertained due to the following: a. Receivables totaling P276.143 million were recorded in total amount without SL details or supporting documentation to substantiate the composition of the balances; b. Unsupported balances of Inter-Agency Receivables amounting to P23.682 million; c. Misclassified tax credits amounting to P510.615 million in the Other Receivables - Others account and unrecorded Other Receivables amounting to P770.569 million; and d. Unreconciled balance of P9.309 million due to non-recording of cleared dishonored checks under the Other Receivables - Dishonored Checks account. These are contrary to Paragraph 27 of the IPSAS 1; Sections 111 and 112 of PD No. 1445; and Items 6.1 and 6.2 of COA Circular No. 2016-005, dated December 19, 2016.

rows.recommendation: We recommended that Management require: a.The OCAT to: •Maintain SLs for all receivable accounts to ensure that detailed records support the bulk amounts reflected in the financial statements. •Immediately coordinate and reconcile with the concerned NGAs and GOCCs to confirm the unconfirmed balances and establish the correct amount for the affected accounts. •Prepare adjusting entries to correct misstatements identified upon thorough evaluation of the transactions Conduct a regular review and reconciliation of receivables, including monthly or quarterly reporting, to ensure the accuracy of balances in the financial statements; and Coordinate and reconcile with the Patrimonial Unit of the City General Services Office's (CGSO) to establish the correct balances for the leased properties of the City
rows.action_plan: The MUSO undertake to faithfully submit a complete and up-to-date schedule of receivables, including collections and ageing reports pertaining to Land-for-the-Landless Program, to OCAT on a timely basis.

observations.summary: The balance of the RPT and Special Education Tax (SET) Receivable amounting to P15.773 billion and P10.888 billion, respectively, as of December 31, 2024, cannot be ascertained due to the following: a. The RPT and SET Receivables per books do not tally with the total RPT Delinquencies recorded in the Real Property Tax Owners Delinquency Listing (RPTODL) by P1.207 billion, due to non-coordination between the OCAT and CTO, which resulted in unreconciled data, contrary to Paragraph 27 of IPSAS 1; and b. No reasonable Allowance for Impairment was provided for RPT and SET Receivables despite the presence of balances that have remained outstanding for more than 30 years totaling P10.888 billion and P5.754 billion for RPT and SET, respectively, which is not in accordance with Paragraph 37 of IPSAS 3 to attain fair presentation as provided by IPSAS 1. These have casted doubt on the accuracy, validity and reliability of the RPT and SET Receivable account balances.

rows.recommendation: We recommended and Management agreed and acted upon on the recommendations to: a. Require the CTO to provide the OCAT with RPTODL for monitoring purposes; b. Direct the OCAT and the CTO to coordinate and reconcile discrepancies between recorded balances of RPT and SET Receivable accounts against the total amount of tax delinquencies indicated in the RPTODL;
rows.action_plan: The OCAT will reconcile the discrepancies and will coordinate closely with the CTO for review, analysis and reconciliation of these accounts. They also committed to undertake a comprehensive assessment of uncollected tax accounts
rows.citation: CY 2024 APMT, CY 2024 Observation No. 4, p. 3
CY 2024 APMT, CY 2024 Observation No. 4, p. 3

rows.recommendation: c. Direct the OCAT to make a reliable estimate of the City's bad debts arising from uncollected taxes and set up an allowance for impairment based on the most reliable and available data that the OCAT can obtain;
rows.citation: CY 2024 APMT, CY 2024 Observation No. 4, p. 3

rows.recommendation: d. Require the OCAT to conduct regular and periodic verification, analysis, and validation of receivable accounts; and e. Ensure strict adherence to the provisions of Section 37 of IPSAS 3-Accounting Policies, Changes in Accounting Estimates and Errors in establishing estimates and sufficient proper disclosures to sustain the fair presentation of financial statements under IPSAS 1

observations.summary: The tax collection strategies and remedies for RPT and SET delinquencies provided under pertinent Sections of RA No. 7160 were not optimally utilized by the City, as manifested by the following circumstances: a. 12,680 Notices of Delinquencies were not received by or served to registered owners of RPUs due to non-updating of addresses and other pertinent information in the RPT Assessment Roll (RPTAR) and Tax Declarations (TDs); b. Submission of a certified list of RPT delinquencies to the City Council and posting of Notice of Delinquencies (NOD) were not undertaken by the CTO within City Hall premises and in strategic locations in barangays where the delinquent RPUS are situated; and c. Discrepancies noted between the TDs vis-à-vis the actual status of properties based on the Geographical Information System (GIS) of the CTO. These conditions contributed to the accumulation of tax delinquencies totaling P27.864 billion, exclusive of interest, as of December 31, 2024, thus, depriving the City of essential income for the implementation of priority PPAs for the benefit of its constituents.

rows.action_plan: The DOA will undertake to comply with the recommendations. In fact, to address the concerns in the AOM, the DOA has already coordinated with the pertinent offices and bureaus of the City to promptly act on the same. observations.summary: The accuracy of the inventory account, totaling P309.908 million, as presented in the FS could not be determined due to: a. Adjustments to year-end balances with net amount of P757.257 million without corresponding documentation; b. Unreconciled differences between the OCAT records and the CGSO Reports of Physical Count of Inventories (RPCI) resulting in misclassification or misposting within Inventory sub-accounts amounting to P301.743 million; c. Inability of the OCAT to maintain Stock Ledger Cards (SLC); and d. Unreliability of the CGSO RPCI due to discrepancies between CGSO reports and hospitals concerned caused by: (1) Incorrect cut-off; (2) non-maintenance of stock cards; and (3) Inconsistencies in the preparation and submission of Summary of Supplies and Materials Issued (SSMI). These are not in accordance with Paragraph 44 of IPSAS 12, Section 114 of the Manual of the New Government Accounting System (MNGAS) for Local Government Units (LGUs), and Section 111 of PD No. 1445.

rows.recommendation: We recommended that: a. The OCAT to- • Provide documentation for inventory adjustment when reconciling the RPCI with accounting records; • Strictly implement the Perpetual Inventory Metho through maintenance of SLC;
rows.action_plan: The OCAT is already working with the CGSO and the Inventory Team for the conduct and completion of the one-time cleansing of PPE. The double recording was already adjusted. They commit to ensure the establishment of the CIPLC for each project simultaneously with the one-time cleansing. Particular attention shall he given to the
rows.remarks: Ongoing coordination among the OCAT, CGSO, Inventory Committee and other concerned offices for the conduct and completion of the one-time cleansing of PPE
rows.citation: CY 2024 APMT, CY 2024 Observation No. 6, p. 3
CY 2024 APMT, CY 2024 Observation No. 6, p. 3

rows.recommendation: • Coordinate with CGSO on the reconciliation and review of Inventory accounts, to include the proper classification of inventories; and • Subsequently, prepare adjusting entries to correct the balances of inventory accounts based on reconciliations conducted. b. The CGSO to - • Observe proper cut-off procedures to ensure that th RPCI reflects correct year-end balances; • Maintain and update stock cards for all Inventory items and ensure that the same are readily available for examination; • Standardize the preparation and submission of SSMI and • Explore the acquisition of an automated Inventor system. c. For hospitals to submit and reconcile their records with CGSO on a regular basis.
rows.action_plan: Particular attention shall be given to the reinforcement of the internal processes, improvement of inter-office collaboration, and pursuit of any supplementary measures that may facilitate the accurate and prompt submission of requisite documents. Furthermore, they justified that the discrepancy was due to the different operational procedures of the two offices - namely, the accounting treatment applied by the OCAT and the technical monitoring and reporting methods they observed. Nonetheless, they are in close coordination with the OCAT to confirm the source of discrepancy and to ensure appropriate adjustments.

observations.summary: The audit of the Land account disclosed the following conditions: a. There are 348 land titles in the custody of the CGSO that are not registered under the name of the City, thus raising uncertainties in the ownership or rightful claim for said real properties; b. The Land Transfer Certificate Titles (TCTs) of the City could not be traced to OCAT and CGSO records due to incomplete details in the Report on the Physical Count of Property, Plant and Equipment (RPCPPE) and SL of the Land account; c. The AO in charge of the custody and safekeeping of the TCTs and vault is not covered with fidelity bond; and d. The vault for TCTs is no longer suitable for safekeeping purposes due to flood damage, and wear and tear. These conditions are contrary to Paragraphs 27 of the IPSAS 1, Section 376 of RA No. 7160 or Local Government Code (LGC), and Section 4.4 of Treasury Circular No. 02-2009. Thus, the accuracy, reliability and existence of the land could not be ascertained. Further, the absence of fidelity bond of the AO and the lack of a suitable vault for TCTs exposes said documents to potential loss, misappropriation, and damage due to natural hazards.

rows.recommendation: We recommended and Management agreed and acted upon on the following: a. The OCAT to coordinate with CGSO to initiate the reconciliation of the land account details and to establish a fair presentation of the account in the books; b. The CGSO to: •Gather data to complete land records and update the inventory listing of land titles; •Secure a fidelity bond for the accountable officer in charge of the safekeeping of the land titles; and •Request the assistance of the Legal Department in evaluating and transferring the TCTs under the name of the City; c. The City Budget Office (CBO) to source funds for the procurement of a safety vault and for possible costs of ownership transfer should several properties be deemed as owned by the City. d. Strictly comply with the proper recording of PPE accounts guided by Paragraphs 27 of IPSAS 1, Paragraph 82 of IPSAS 17, Section 125 of the MNGAS, Section 376 of RA No. 7160 and Section 4.4 of Treasury Circular No. 2-2009.
rows.action_plan: The OCAT is collaborating with the CGSO to reconcile the account. The CGSO is currently gathering data to establish and maintain an exhaustive, authoritative, and verifiable repository of land assets. Likewise, they have identified a suitable location for the vault and preparatory activities is presently being undertaken such as minor retrofitting and fixture adjustments to ensure readiness upon delivery and installation of the vault. The requisite bond covering the accountable officer is currently on process and has been documented by Special Order dated April 10, 2025. The GCSO will actively and continually engage with the City Legal Office to facilitate transfer transactions and documentation.
rows.status_text: Not implemented Not implemented Not implemented Not implemented Not implemented Not implemented
rows.remarks: Ongoing coordination with OCAT, CGSO, and City Legal Office -do- -do-

observations.summary: The following practices are not in accordance with Paragraph 66 of the IPSAS 17, and Sections 4.12 to 4.14, 5.7 to 5.8, 6 and 7 of COA Circular 2015-008 dated November 23, 2015: a. Non-recognition of the depreciation expense and accumulated depreciation on the Infrastructure Assets (IA) - Road Networks account with a total cost of P2.32 billion; b. Non-preparation of the Report on Local Road Network due to the absence of data, such as the complete description and cost segregation of road components for the road projects coming from the DEPW; and c. Non-maintenance of the subsidiary records on components of road networks. Thus, the existence, accuracy, and validity of the balances of the IA - Road Networks account and its corresponding Depreciation Expense and Accumulated Depreciation account could not be established.

rows.recommendation: We recommended that Management require: a. The DEPW to provide OCAT and CGSO complete information of IA-Road Networks, including road IDs, road names, components, descriptions, and cost segregation, to enable the accurate preparation of reports such as the Report on Local Road Network and the Report on Physical Count of the Road Network;
rows.action_plan: The CGSO stated that the City issued a memorandum directing the Inventory Committee to conduct a comprehensive Local Road inventory and Road mapping. The OCAT commented that the physical count of all road network assets is still ongoing
rows.citation: CY 2024 APMT, CY 2024 Observation No. 8, p. 4

rows.recommendation: b.The OCAT to: • Coordinate with DEPW and CGSO to establish th estimated useful life of the depreciable component of road networks and identify road lots; • Coordinate with CGSO to determine the acquisitio date for items with incomplete information and update the Road Network Lapsing Schedule; • Recognize the depreciation and accumulate depreciation for the items under road networks using the prescribed chart of accounts; and • Comply with Sections 4 to 8 of COA Circular No. 2015 008, Paragraph 27 IPSAS 1, Paragraph 59 of IPSAS 17.
rows.status_text: Not Implemented Not Implemented Not Implemented Not Implemented
rows.citation: CY 2024 APMT, CY 2024 Observation No. 8, p. 5

rows.recommendation: c. The Inventory Committee to conduct a comprehensive physical Inventory of all road network assets; d. The CGSO to prepare the Report on the Local Road Network and the Inventory Committee to submit the Report on the Physical Count of the Local Road Network in accordance with Section VI and VII-b of COA Circular No. 2015-008; e. The DEPW, CGSO and OCAT to enhance coordination regarding IA-Road Networks; and f. The City to comply with pertinent provisions of COA Circular No. 2015-008, Paragraphs 27 of the IPSAS 1, Paragraph 59 of IPSAS 17.
rows.status_text: Not Implemented Not Implemented Not Implemented Not Implemented

observations.summary: 9. The balances of the Building and School Buildings account as of December 31, 2024, cannot be ascertained due to the following: a. Discrepancies between the OCAT SLs and the CGSO RPCPPE amounting to P3.741 billion due to: • PPE items that were recorded In the OCAT but not In the RPCPP amounting to PO.772 billion; • PPE items that were recorded in the RPCPPE but not in the OCA totaling P4.512 billion; These conditions are not in accordance with Paragraph 27 of the IPSAS 1, Paragraph 82 of IPSAS 17, Section 147 of COA Circular 92-386, and Section 3.6 of COA Circular 2020-006. These discrepancies between the OCAT and CGSO records cast doubt on the accuracy, reliability and validity of the reported balances of Building and School Buildings. Also, the non-derecognition of demolished PPE overstated the School Buildings account by P0.051 billion.

rows.recommendation: 9.14.We recommended that Management direct: a. The OCAT and CGSO to initiate reconciliation of their date; b. The OCAT to coordinate with the DEPW and establish the cost of demolished school buildings for proper derecognition in the books (with supporting documentation);
rows.action_plan: Management planned on implementing the one-time cleansing of PPE. Simultaneously, CGSO will Initiate coordination with the DEPW and formally request the submission of all relevant documentation relative to the demolition of school buildings, to facilitate the verification of reported adjustments and proper attribution of asset status
rows.remarks: Ongoing coordination among the OCAT, CGSO, Inventory Committee and other concerned offices for the conduct and completion of the one-time cleansing of PPE

rows.recommendation: c. The DEPW to fast-track the retrieval of documents pertaining to demolished school buildings, and submit to OCAT and CGSO verified Information for updating purposes; and d. Strictly comply with Paragraphs 27 of IPSAS 1, Paragraph 82 of IPSAS 17, Section 147 of COA Circular 92-386 and Section 6.3 of COA Circular No. 2020-006.
rows.citation: CY 2024 APMT, CY 2024 Observation No. 9, p. 5

observations.summary: 10. The reliability and completeness of the PPE - Medical Equipment account balance totaling P1.825 billion could not be ascertained due to the following: a. Discrepancies between the OCAT SLs and the CGSO RPCPPE amounting to P1.181 billion, due to: •PPE items recorded in the OCAT but not in the RPCPPE amounting to PO.776 billion; • PPE items that were recorded in the RPCPPE but not in the OCA totaling P2.017 billion; • PPE items amounting to P0.061 billion that could not be reconcile due to insufficient data or description on both records; and b. PPE items amounting to P0.174 billion were incorrectly classified under the Medical Equipment account. These are not in accordance with Paragraph 27 of the IPSAS 1, and Section 6.3 of COA Circular No. 2020-006. These discrepancies between the OCAT and CGSO records adversely affected the accuracy and validity of the reported balances of PPE-Medical Equipment Also, the misclassification overstated the Medical Equipment account by P0.174 billion and understated the Computer Software account, together with its Accumulated Depreciation of P0.003 billion, and Prior Period Adjustment account for the Semi-Expendable Items amounting to P0.170 billion.

rows.recommendation: 10.11.We recommended that Management direct: a.The OCAT to: • Coordinate with the CGSO to address inconsistencies i the PPE items and properly account for them in the accounting records; • Prepare the necessary information required by CO Circular No. 2020-006, and conduct the procedures provided therein for the implementation of the one-time cleansing of PPE in the books; and • Prepare adjusting entries to correct the misclassifie Medical Equipment items.
rows.action_plan: The OCAT committed that beginning CY 2025, their office is working with the CGSO and the Inventory Team for the conduct and completion of the one-time cleansing of PPE. Also, JEV No. 1002501008778 was drawn in CY 2025 to address observation B. The CGSO will prepare and provide all available necessary documents needed by the OCAT in order to update their SLs based on RPCPPE report of 2024 and inventory results of the one-time cleansing, based and guided by COA Circular 2020-006
rows.status_text: Not Implemented Not Implemented Not Implemented
rows.remarks: Ongoing coordination among the OCAT, CGSO, Inventory Committee and other concerned offices for the conduct and completion of the one-time cleansing of PPE
rows.citation: CY 2024 APMT, CY 2024 Observation No. 10, p. 5

rows.recommendation: b. The CGSO to: • Coordinate with the OCAT for the reconciliation of PPE records against the RPCPPE, and address issues pertaining to PPEs found at stations during the physical count; and • Prepare the requirements per COA Circular No. 2020-006 and expedite the procedures outlined therein for the one-time cleansing of PPE.
rows.citation: CY 2024 APMT, CY 2024 Observation No. 10, p. 6

rows.recommendation: c. Henceforth, strictly comply with the proper recording of PPE accounts as guided by Paragraph 14 of IPSAS 1, and Section 6.3 of COA Circular No. 2020-006.

observations.summary: 11. The six City District Hospitals could not maximize utilization of their resources due to the following PPE and Semi-Expendable Items challenges that have not been addressed: a. Unserviceable PPE and Semi-Expendable Items amounting to P74.131 million remained undisposed; b. Unserviceable PPE and Semi-Expendable items amounting to P45.867 million could no longer be traced in the books despite non-disposal of said items; and c. Semi-expandable property items that are no longer used and unserviceable amounting to P1.128 million were inappropriately reported in the Waste Materials Report (WMR). These are contrary to Part I, Section C.1 of COA-DBM Joint Circular No. 2024-1 dated January 30, 2024, or the Revised Manual on the Disposal of Government Properties, Section 4.7.10 of COA Circular No. 2022-004 dated May 30, 2022, and Section 167 of COA Circular No. 92-386, dated October 20, 1992, or the Rules and Regulations In the Supply and Property Management in the Local Governments

rows.recommendation: 11.16.We recommended that Management require the: a. Disposal Committee and CGSO coordinate with the Property Units of the six District Hospitals to facilitate the procedures for disposal of items and updating of the IIRUP and WMR, as guided by COA-DBM Joint Circular No. 2024-1, Section 4.7.10 of COA Circular No. 2022-004 and Section 167 of COA Circular No. 92-386;
rows.action_plan: The CGSO stated that they coordinated with the 6 district hospitals and assisted them with the classifications, proper procedures and other modes of disposal of unserviceable PPE and semi-expendables. In addition, they also disseminated memorandum dated May 9, 2025 informing all departments on the proper procedures and appropriate forms in compliance with JC No. 2024-1, COA Circular 2022-004 and COA Circular 92-386.
rows.action_taken: CGSO disseminated memorandum dated May 9, 2025 informing all departments on the proper procedures and appropriate forms In compliance with JC No. 2024-1, COA Circular 2022-004 and COA Circular 92-386.

OCAT to revisit and reconcile all adjusting entries made in prior years pertaining to the dropping of PPE accounts in the books to account for the items that are no longer recorded; and

observations.summary: 12. The reliability and accuracy of the Construction In Progress (CIP) account balance totaling P4.086 billion cannot be ascertained due to: a. Non-reconciliation of the OCAT records and the CGSO RPCPPE of the CIP, with discrepancies amounting to P6.532 billion due to: • Projects appearing in the RPCPPE of CIP but were not recorded in th books, amounting to P0.106 billion; • Projects that have been completed but remain recorded under C and have not yet been reclassified to their corresponding asset accounts amounting to P2.097 billion; • The CIP account is credited for completed projects. However, th corresponding debit entry to initially recognize the project was not recorded, amounting to P0.241 billion; and •Double recording of transactions amounting to P0.178 billion. b. Non-maintenance of the CIP Ledger Card (CIPLC) for each project by the OCAT. These practices are not in accordance with Paragraph 27 of the IPSAS 1, Section 16 of Chapter 1 of Volume II of the MNGAS for LGUs, and Section 111 of PD No.1445. Thus, the fairness of the CIP account balance could not be established.

rows.recommendation: 12.18. We recommended that Management direct the OCAT to: a. Analyze the CIP account and make appropriate adjustments to attain its fair presentation; b. Regularly coordinate with CGSO and other Implementing offices to timely recognize the completion of projects and consider the formulation of guidelines that will address issues such as delayed processing of final billings by contractors to facilitate the timely and proper accounting treatment of CIP transactions; and
rows.action_plan: The OCAT is already working with the CGSO and the Inventory Team for the conduct and completion of the one-time cleansing of PPE. The double recording was already adjusted. They commit to ensure the establishment of the CIPLC for each project simultaneously with the one-time cleansing. The CGSO conveys it readiness to further enhance the coordination with concerned departments to ensure the timely and proper recognition of completed projects. observations.summary: 14. The Due to BIR account amounting to P577.243 million could not be established due to the existence of: a. Unremitted/unreconciled taxes withheld, including those from prior years amounting to P491.145 million, which is not in compliance with BIR revenue regulations; and b. rows.recommendation: 14.18. We recommended that the Management direct the OCAT to: a. Maintain a record that monitors the status of any unpaid employee compensation where taxes are already withheld; and c. The gaps in procedures and policies expose the City and its employees to unnecessary interest and affect the employees' loan privileges and other benefits from the GSIS.

rows.recommendation: 15.18.We recommended and Management agreed to: a.Require the DPOs to: • Ensure the timely submission of updated information of City employees to GSIS, such as new salary rates, employment status, positions, and other pertinent information to minimize the occurrence of mismatched records; • Promptly address deficiencies noted which cause the mismatch of data, and coordinate/report to the CPO all actions taken and results of such actions regarding the request for updates of employees' Information before the GSIS; and
rows.action_plan: The CPO stated that the recommendations are well considered. rows.recommendation: 23.7. We recommended that Management require the CCPC to: a. Adopt the provisions of the DILG MC Nos. 2021-039 and 2008-126.

observations.summary: 24. The following challenges In the implementation of the Ecological Solid Waste Management (ESWM) Act of 2000 or RA No. 9003 continue to burden the City's effective realization of the benefits of said law, to wit: a. Insufficient updating of pertinent ordinances and the SWM Plan to address the evolving conditions In the City; b. Program goals to promote awareness through Information Education Campaign (IEC) for commercial establishments were not accomplished, and targets for growth were not adjusted to consider demographic shifts; c. The Manila City Environment and Natural Resources Office (CENRO) has yet to be established. The aforementioned circumstances have adversely affected the City's enforcement of the ESWM Act of 2000.

rows.recommendation: We recommended that Management: a. Through the DPS and SWM Board, for SWM ordinances and SWM Plans, to: • Fast-track the revision of outdated SWM ordinance and strengthen penalties for non-compliance to align with evolving national policies and current environmental challenges of the City; and • Formulate a mechanism for the regular review and updating of the SWM Plan to ensure compliance with legal requirements and responsiveness to evolving waste management challenges. b. Implement aggressive IEC campaigns to increase public awareness and compliance, and adjust engagement targets to reflect demographic changes. c. Direct the City Council to take the necessary steps to operationalize the Manila CENRO to fulfill its environmental mandate.
rows.action_plan: DPS will propose to the City Solid Waste Management Board at least once a year update on the PPAs Indicated In the plan as part of Its monitoring and evaluation mechanism to form part of the regular updates of the SWM Plan. DPS will formulate a robust IEC strategy that will utilize multiple communication platforms such as social media, digital channels, community engagement, and flyers.
rows.citation: CY 2024 APMT, CY 2024 Observation No. 24, p. 10

observations.summary: 26. The City's implementation of the Local Climate Change Action Pla (LCCAP) cannot be ascertained due to the following conditions: a.
